IUJ strongly recommends applying in the 1st or 2nd intake for scholarship consideration and states applicants in the 3rd intake are extremely unlikely to be nominated for a full scholarship.
official.status_note: IUJ's Admissions page publishes the September 2027 Admission Schedule for International Applicants with the 1st, 2nd and 3rd application rounds still ahead as of the verification date; IUJ notes that scholarship information is subject to change.

application_method: Read the Admissions Guidelines and Scholarship Guidelines published in Brochures & Admissions Materials

official.application_route: One submission only: the two-phase IUJ Online Application, with the scholarship request made in the Phase 2 Scholarship Section; there is no separate scholarship application, form or interview.
official.citizenship_residency: Published for non-Japanese applicants: 'Non-Japanese IUJ applicants who do not have sufficient funds to attend IUJ can apply'. Category A also states both domestic (residents of Japan, regardless of nationality) and international applicants are eligible to be nominated. Non-Japanese recipients must hold a Japan Student Visa status.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is published for non-Japanese (international) applicants; residents of Japan are also eligible for this Category A award regardless of nationality
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No nationality or field-of-study restriction for Nakayama Premium itself; the applicant must be admitted to an eligible IUJ programme (GSIR: IRP, IDP, JGDP (MA), PMPP, IPPP; GSIM: MBA, JGDP (MBA), IMBA, DXP; PhD: Economics, Public Management or International Relations cluster)
official.research_requirement: GSIR admission applicants submit a Research Topic of 500-700 words for the proposed IUJ thesis; GSIM applicants follow the published Research Topic template. These are admission requirements considered in the screening that decides the scholarship.
official.duration: Master's programmes: one academic year (IPPP, IMBA, DXP) or two academic years (IRP, IDP, JGDP (MA), PMPP, MBA, JGDP (MBA)); PhD programme: three years. The Nakayama Premium is a one-year scholarship, with extension for the second year on a commendable record (PhD: a second extension for the 3rd year is possible based on performance over the first two years).
official.description: The S. Nakayama Memorial Scholarship Premium (Nakayama Premium) is IUJ's top direct award: IUJ provides a limited number of scholarships for newly enrolling international students to support their IUJ studies with the expectation that they will also be active participants in support of the local community and gain a good understanding of Japanese society. Scholars are expected to develop leadership skills and contribute to international society in a leadership role upon graduation. It covers full tuition, most of the admissions fee, and a monthly stipend.
official.region: Asia (IUJ campus, 777 Kokusai-cho, Minami Uonuma-shi, Niigata, Japan)
official.program_type: IUJ Direct Award Scholarship (Category A: announced along with IUJ admissions decisions)
official.english_requirement: An official TOEFL (iBT, institution code 0712; TOEFL-ITP not accepted), IELTS (Academic module) or TOEIC score is required unless exempt: Category 1 - English-medium education for at least four years during secondary studies in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the U.K. or the U.S.A., regardless of nationality; Category 2 - completed (or expected) undergraduate or graduate degree at an institution where the language of instruction is English, with evidence issued by the degree-granting institution (a transcript is acceptable only if it clearly states the language of instruction is English). Scores are valid if obtained within 2 years prior to application.

applicant_utility.summary: The Nakayama Premium is IUJ's most generous admission-linked award for privately funded non-Japanese applicants: full tuition, 250,000 yen off the 300,000 yen admissions fee, and a 100,000 yen monthly stipend. There is no separate scholarship application - your admission file is the scholarship file, and the decision is announced with your admission result. Apply in the 1st intake (2nd at the latest) because IUJ warns that 3rd-intake applicants are extremely unlikely to be nominated for a full scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically strong, privately funded non-Japanese applicants to GSIR or GSIM Master's programmes or the GSIR PhD who can hit the November/December 2026 first-round deadlines and meet IUJ's interview and English requirements.
application_readiness_checklist: Register in the IUJ Online Application System with sponsorship status 'Non-Sponsored' - sponsored applicants are not considered for this scholarship
Complete the Phase 2 Scholarship Section deliberately; skipping it means you are not in the scholarship pool at all
Book TOEFL/IELTS early - scores must be under 2 years old and IUJ advises allowing 4-5 weeks for score delivery before the deadline
Get transcripts and degree certificates officially stamped/signed; if issued in another language, have a professional English translation prepared
Budget the 50,000 yen admissions-fee balance and one-off move-in costs (10,000 yen dormitory maintenance fee) before the first payment deadline
Keep the GSIM interview date free (it cannot be changed; submitting GMAT/GRE removes the interview requirement)
common_rejection_risks: Applying in the 3rd intake, when full-scholarship nomination is described as extremely unlikely
Registering as government/company-sponsored, or omitting the Phase 2 Scholarship Section, which removes you from consideration entirely
An average academic record - Nakayama Premium is reserved for the most capable candidates, so weaker profiles tend to be slotted into the lower Nakayama tiers instead
Assuming you can choose or appeal the award: scholarships are assigned by the Admissions Committee based on the admissions outcome
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to Japan and personal travel (not covered), the 50,000 yen admissions-fee balance, dormitory maintenance fee (10,000 yen at move-in), utilities, meals, books and academic supplies, insurance and National Health Insurance contributions, and social/personal expenses. IUJ's own published budget estimate for a single student's first academic year is roughly 4.5-5.3 million yen in total, of which tuition is exempted under this award.
document_audit: Certificates without the institution's stamp or registrar signature are rejected outright
A transcript alone does not prove English-medium instruction for the exemption - you need separate evidence issued by the degree-granting institution
TOEFL-ITP is not accepted, and IELTS must be taken as the Academic module (General Training reading/writing sections do not qualify)
GSIR applicants need both a 400-600 word Personal Statement and a separate 500-700 word Research Topic; GSIM applicants use the GSIM research-topic template instead
A residence card copy is required only from non-Japanese domestic applicants - do not confuse it with the passport copy all applicants must upload
alerts: The 100,000 yen monthly stipend is terminated if you subsequently receive any other monthly living stipend except JASSO
Recipients are in principle housed in IUJ dormitories and asked to support dorm life in a 'work-study' arrangement, with no priority in room assignment

Category A recipients cannot apply for an upgraded scholarship after enrolling, and tuition must still be paid by 31 August or dismissal can follow - the exemption is applied through IUJ's procedure, so watch the payment deadlines
The award is one year at a time: renewal for year 2 (and year 3 for PhD) depends on maintaining a commendable academic record
Most IUJ scholarships require recipients to hold a Japan Student Visa; IUJ assists successful applicants in obtaining this status
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single online submission through the two-phase IUJ application with the scholarship request embedded in Phase 2; admission interview (where required) and the scholarship decision follow in the admission result announcement.
